steps.what: Select current sociology sources and examples for the lesson
Prepare sociology explanations and classroom activities

loop.purpose: Draft source-grounded explanations and activity variants
loop.output: Draft material with explicit source references
loop.check: The sociologist checks factual claims, theoretical framing and activity suitability against the sources and objectives.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported claims or unsuitable activities return to manual preparation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Existing materials are reused first; new explanations and activity wording require context-specific drafting.

steps.what: Check lesson accuracy, examples and suitability for the students
Teach sociology and respond to students' questions

tasks.design: Use native {LMS} and {DOCS} source views, then a bounded drafting loop for the teaching material already prepared today. The sociologist checks the theoretical content and retains classroom explanation, discussion and student response.
tasks.previous_blocker: New lesson material can require repeated source restatement and activity wording.
tasks.enabler_now: Selected course sources can ground checked drafting without automatic assessment of students.
tasks.still_hard: Contested theories and students' misunderstandings require responsive teaching.
tasks.human_edge: Explain different interpretations and recognise what students have understood.
tasks.altitude: Shift some preparation effort toward evaluating explanations and teaching responsively.

reach.learn: Check activities against actual learning objectives.

evidence.claim: Source-grounded drafting could reduce repeated preparation; teaching and the proposed saving remain an unmeasured human-led scenario.

assumptions: The baseline includes teaching material already used by students, with no new attendance log or trailing report. Grading is not part of this task.

The sociologist supplies learning objectives and selects source versions and examples in s1. Its retained time includes capture and checking; missing or unsuitable sources return to manual preparation.
Native source views remove only 2 hours of repeated navigation. The separate draft step reduces source restatement and wording, retaining content judgement and the full classroom session.
Reuse existing lessons first. Ordinary author saves remain retained without self-approval.
unknowns: How much current preparation is genuinely new rather than reused.
research_questions: Time complete preparation including source checks and corrections for several sociology lessons.

already_counted.description: Check lesson accuracy and teach students

incremental.description: Maintain source grounding and lesson drafting checks

approvals.approved_version: Exact teaching material and statements delivered to the current students; changed claims require checking before presentation.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=88, gross 12 minus 3 upkeep gives central net 9. Conservative case: poor source indexing retains all 10 source hours and difficult theoretical framing retains 22/25 preparation hours plus 65 fixed: 97 retained, 3 gross minus 3 =0. Suitable sources and reusable activity patterns retain 9 source and 18 preparation hours plus 65 fixed: 92 retained, 8 gross minus 3 =5.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan and conduct research testing sociological theories

steps.what: Define societal research questions, theory and defensible study design
Write the research protocol and analysis specification
outputs: protocol with variables, sampling and analysis rules

steps.what: Conduct research and capture checked observations or responses
inputs: protocol with variables, sampling and analysis rules

steps.what: Calculate specified analyses for the theory tests
inputs: protocol with variables, sampling and analysis rules

steps.what: Interpret the evidence and assess implications for the theory
Write the study findings and limitations with analysis provenance

tasks.design: Use native {DOCS} protocol headings and tested {DATA_PLATFORM} calculations for analyses specified by the sociologist. Retain design, real data collection and capture, interpretation and substantive scientific writing.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated protocol sections and rebuilt calculations can sit alongside original research.
tasks.enabler_now: Explicit specifications and tested analysis routines support reproducibility without automatic theory choice.
tasks.still_hard: Sampling, construct validity and competing explanations require scientific judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Ask a meaningful question and determine what the evidence can support.
tasks.altitude: Make repeatable analysis explicit while retaining original sociological inquiry.

reach.learn: Keep source, variable definitions and exclusions traceable.

evidence.claim: The digest reports that synthetic respondents varied less than real respondents and drifted; this design retains actual research data rather than replacing participants.
Tested analyses and native protocol headings could reduce repeated work; savings for this study are unmeasured.

assumptions: The boundary includes the plan, data capture, analysis and scientific findings record, without adding a new activity log. A qualitative project without specified repeatable calculations has a different eligible baseline.

The sociologist produces variable definitions, sampling, exclusions and analysis rules in s2. S3 retains the full time to collect and enter identified observations, dates, values and source provenance, including consent/access checks in the current research process. Missing or inconsistent records return to manual reconciliation before s4.

Protocol headings remove 3 hours of repeated required-field structure. Findings headings remove only 1 hour of provenance formatting because scientific conclusions remain individual. Existing scripted analyses supply no new calculation saving.
No synthetic participants, automatic individual assessment or external publication is proposed. Ordinary saves stay retained without self-approval.
unknowns: How much current analysis is repeatable and not already scripted.
Whether the protocol and findings record have reusable structures.
research_questions: Replay a completed study and distinguish original design, capture, repeated calculation and writing effort.

already_counted.description: Conduct research and interpret scientific validity

incremental.description: Maintain analysis tests and protocol/provenance headings

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=76, gross 24 minus 4 upkeep gives central net 20. Conservative case: unusual design retains 14/15 protocol hours, bespoke analyses retain 17/20 calculation hours and incomplete output metadata retain 9/10 findings hours plus 55 fixed: 95 retained, 5 gross minus 4 =1. A compatible recurring design retains 13 protocol, 7 calculation and 9 findings hours plus 55 fixed: 84 retained, 16 gross minus 4 =12.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Present research findings at professional meetings

steps.what: Select the research findings and evidence for the professional audience
Draft the research presentation's argument and explanation

loop.purpose: Draft an explanation of the selected findings
loop.output: Draft presentation text with linked evidence
loop.check: The sociologist checks each finding, qualification and source reference against the actual study.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported interpretations or unresolved references return to manual drafting.
loop.why_not_simpler: Layout is deterministic, but constructing the spoken argument requires context-specific language.

steps.what: Check the presentation's findings, citations and limitations
Format checked presentation content in the meeting's slide layout
Present research findings and answer professional questions

tasks.design: Prepare source-grounded presentation content in {DOCS} through a bounded drafting loop, followed by deterministic slide formatting. The sociologist selects and checks the findings, checks the exact formatted presentation before delivery and retains professional discussion.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rephrasing findings for a meeting and formatting slides can repeat existing research material.
tasks.enabler_now: A selected evidence packet can ground draft text while native layouts handle formatting separately.
tasks.still_hard: The presenter must communicate uncertainty and respond to methodological challenges.
tasks.human_edge: Defend the argument and recognise the limits of the findings.
tasks.altitude: Spend presentation effort on a defensible argument and discussion.

reach.learn: Keep each presented claim linked to the study evidence.

evidence.claim: The digest reports a government report with fabricated references and a partial refund; this supports checking references, not a presentation time-saving claim.

assumptions: Presentation writing and formatting are part of the actual current preparation, with no added meeting report or activity log.

The sociologist supplies selected findings, table versions, limitations and resolvable references in s1, fully retaining that selection and capture time. Missing evidence returns the relevant claim to manual checking.
Native slide layouts are tried before custom formatting. S4 removes real formatting, not the author's same-system save. No automatic conference submission or publication is implied.
The final delivery gate covers the formatted version, including any layout changes affecting meaning.
unknowns: How much existing material is already ready to present.
Whether native layouts preserve study figures and qualifications.
research_questions: Compare full preparation and correction time for presentations with complex tables and caveats.

already_counted.description: Check evidence and deliver the professional presentation

incremental.description: Maintain drafting checks and presentation layouts

approvals.approved_version: Exact formatted slides, figures, citations and spoken findings for this meeting; changes require checking again before delivery.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=76, gross 24 minus 3 upkeep gives central net 21. Conservative case: difficult argumentation retains 32/35 writing hours and incompatible figure layouts retain 8/10 formatting hours plus 55 fixed: 95 retained, 5 gross minus 3 =2. Suitable source content and compatible layouts retain 26 writing and 3 formatting hours plus 55 fixed: 84 retained, 16 gross minus 3 =13.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Explain sociological research to the public

steps.what: Select sociological findings and source evidence for public explanation
Choose an accessible framing that preserves uncertainty and meaning
Write the public explanation from the chosen evidence and framing

loop.purpose: Draft accessible language from the selected research
loop.input: Selected evidence, audience and chosen framing
loop.output: Draft explanation with source-linked claims and caveats
loop.check: The sociologist checks each claim and example for fidelity to the study and understandable meaning.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported examples, exaggerated findings or missing caveats return to manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Fixed headings cannot provide audience-specific explanations of varied research, but existing text is reused first.

steps.what: Check the explanation for factual accuracy and misleading simplification
Deliver the explanation and respond to the public's questions

tasks.design: Use a bounded {DOCS} drafting loop for the public explanation already prepared today, grounded in findings and framing chosen by the sociologist. Keep evidence selection, simplification judgement, checking and public delivery with the scientist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Converting technical findings into accessible language can require repeated wording work.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded source-grounded draft can propose accessible wording for human checking.
tasks.still_hard: Simplification can erase uncertainty or imply a stronger causal claim than the evidence supports.
tasks.human_edge: Explain contested findings responsibly and respond to the audience's concerns.
tasks.altitude: Reduce wording effort while retaining responsibility for public meaning.

reach.learn: Preserve qualifications while making research understandable.

evidence.claim: Source-grounded drafting could assist public explanations; audience understanding and this task's time saving require validation.

assumptions: The scenario includes an existing prepared explanation actually delivered to the public; spontaneous oral-only answers have no eligible writing baseline. No trailing communication log is added.

The sociologist produces selected finding versions, references and limitations in s1 and audience framing in s2; all source selection and capture time is retained. Missing references or unclear qualifications return to manual preparation.
Reuse existing explanations and native document formats first. No automatic public answer service, unreviewed publication or invented source is proposed.
Ordinary author saves remain retained without self-approval; the delivery gate covers the actual explanation and changed statements.
unknowns: How often current explanations need new wording.
How much draft correction is needed for nuanced findings.
research_questions: Measure writing plus checking time and test whether public readers preserve the study's uncertainty after reading the explanation.

already_counted.description: Check the explanation and deliver it responsively

approvals.approved_version: Exact explanation, source claims and caveats delivered to this public audience; changed wording affecting meaning requires checking again.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=86, gross 14 minus 3 upkeep gives central net 11. Conservative case: contested findings require extensive rewriting and retain 32/35 drafting hours plus 65 fixed: 97 retained, 3 gross minus 3 =0. Clear source metadata and compatible accessible phrasing retain 25 drafting hours plus 65 fixed: 90 retained, 10 gross minus 3 =7.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Keep theoretical judgement, real research and public meaning with sociologists while making repeated preparation and analysis explicit.
reach: Work with research assistants and communicators on traceable sources and findings.
role.ambitious_version: Reproducible research and clear teaching and communication with bounded assistance and accountable interpretation.
